sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## What this repository is

`theta-agent` — a **pi package** (extensions + skills for the [pi](https://pi.dev) coding agent) that grows into **Theta**, a science co-researcher agent for biology/biomedicine. It is the code repo of the Theta campaign; design decisions (T1–T10), milestone definitions, and task handoffs live in the campaign vault (path in `CLAUDE.local.md`). Treat the vault as read-only reference.

Current state: 0.5.0 — M5 is shipped. The M1 base ships the `theta` launcher (a thin `bin/theta.mjs` that runs `pi -e <package-root>`; macOS/Linux — Windows waits for M8, tracked in issue #2) and the Tier-1 library: K-Dense skills vendored verbatim per ADR 0001 plus the self-authored `theta-research-loop` orchestrator, with re-syncs at milestone boundaries (`docs/agents/resync.md`). M2 adds the first connector skill, `theta-lit-search` (PubMed, arXiv, Semantic Scholar), landed tracer-first: search and get-by-identifier with pacing, in-200 error detection, and credential redaction enforced in its scripts (ADR 0002; script invariants in `docs/agents/connector-scripts.md`). M3 adds `theta-notebook`, the project notebook skill (ADR 0003): five dated provenance-entry types with content-addressed, graded evidence snapshots under the research project's `.theta/`, a recorder script under the connector-script invariants, a notebook-written attestation in the dogfood auditor, and orchestrator doctrine weaving recording into all six loop stages. M4 ships the compute gateway `theta-compute` (ADR 0004) from `gateway/` — a FastMCP server wrapping the Slurm CLI with argv arrays only, bearer auth from deploy-time env, one audit JSONL line per tool call, and the seven generic tools (the read-only environments/status pair plus the stage–submit–logs–cancel–fetch lifecycle) behind the path sandbox and the command guard, plus the typed `run_alphafold3` rendering the deploy-time template registry's registered template with its free variables only — all out of the npm tarball. On the theta side, M4 landed the gateway skill's lifecycle doctrine and the submit gate (#54), and the notebook's job-record path (#55): a compute run records a method entry whose evidence item is the assembled gateway job record, graded `re-executed` when its artifacts were fetched, and the orchestrator's execute stage routes cluster jobs to `theta-compute`. M5 stacks the safety gates: the deploy-time submit capability (ADR 0006) and the per-principal submit ceiling on the gateway, and on the theta side the submit gate grown into the stacked gate framework (#95) — the literal three-tool confirm set pinned against the gateway's destructive annotations (disagreement is drift and refuses loudly), concurrency-safe stacked confirms (pi 1.4.0's concurrent-dialog fix is the floor), `parentToolCallId` riding prompts, refusals, and the session-dir gate log (`gate.jsonl`, one JSONL line per gated decision), and the dogfood auditor reading codemode's `nestedCalls` records instead of assuming a flat call sequence. M5 S3 (#96) makes the rig itself gateway-bearing: the clean-room rig admits the gateway token as its second credential (`--gateway`, URL host rewritten to the Docker host alias, preflighted in-container before launch — the token rides a 0600 env file, never argv), a checked-in RPC confirm driver (`test/rig/rpc-driver.mjs`) answers the submit gate for headless `--rpc` evidence legs, the gateway skill carries the capability/throttle/codemode doctrine, the auditor finds the transcript by its own name grammar beside the gate log, and the M5 dogfood (gated submit with confirm, held refusal, throttle) ran in the rig against the live gateway. M6 opens the eval suite (ADR 0007) with the replay net's tracer (#133): a checked-in scenario list (`test/eval/scenarios.mjs`), the typed normalization layer with its five rewrite classes, and one connector fixture — a sanitized rig capture — pinned three ways in the keyless standard suite (provenance: one digest per model-visible surface class, so a model-visible edit reds until a fresh capture; snapshot: the normalized entry tree equals its committed snapshot; determinism: pi's reconstruction yields one context hash), with the capture pipeline (`test/eval/capture.mjs`) and doctrine in `docs/agents/eval.md` — all outside the npm tarball. M6 S1 (#134) extends the net to one fixture per model-visible surface class — orchestrator doctrine, the notebook recorder, the gateway skill, and the extension's user-facing strings (the submit gate's refusal, captured on a `--gateway` rig leg where print mode refuses the submit before any server call) — each with its scenario, sanitized fixture, and the three pins; the per-scenario shape assertion lives in `test/eval/shape.mjs`, and the orchestrator fixture binds the vendored skill its doctrine routes to, so a body-only re-sync reds by name.

## pi-package rules

- Host-provided packages (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`, `@earendil-works/pi-ai`, `@earendil-works/pi-agent-core`, `@earendil-works/pi-tui`, `typebox`) go in `peerDependencies` with `"*"` ranges — never `dependencies`, never bundled.
- Keep the `pi-package` keyword (gallery eligibility) and the explicit `pi` manifest (`extensions`, `skills`) in `package.json`. Manifest fields are arrays of strings — pi silently drops bare-string fields (guarded by `test/manifest.test.mjs`).
- Never install `pi-mcp-adapter` — an installed adapter replaces pi's built-in MCP support (native since pi 0.99).
- Target pi ≥ 1.4.0 and Node ≥ 22.19.0. The floor moves only at milestone boundaries, under the standing adoption rule recorded on #87 — a held review is recorded on the parent spec, never silent. Package loading uses `pi -e <source>`; local-path sources load without copying, so a repo checkout works exactly like the installed package.
- The pi extension API is read from the installed package, not the web — the paths below sit under the pi install root (`$(npm root -g)/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/`): `docs/extensions.md` (events, the tool-call pipeline, UI modes), `docs/mcp.md` (tool naming and exposure — MCP tool names are sanitized to `[A-Za-z0-9_]`, so a server hyphen registers as an underscore), and `dist/core/extensions/types.d.ts` for the exact event and context shapes.

## Conventions

- Conventional commits (`feat:`, `chore:`, `docs:`). Tabs and existing field order in `package.json`.
- Extract a shared helper as soon as the same logic shape appears twice — tree-wide, not per-module: a module boundary created mid-strike is where duplication is born, so the shared shape gets one home before the second caller (tests included). Copying code verbatim is for separately shipped trees only — skill-to-skill, never within a file.
- Failure paths in runner and helper scripts: child-process spawns inherit the environment (overlay onto `process.env`, never replace it — the eslint `spawn-env-inherit` rule enforces direct call sites); `finally` cleanup never masks the primary failure; a machine-readable result lands as a file when its channel is shared with payload output (the exit-status rule — and a pipeline whose exit gates the next step runs unpiped or under `set -o pipefail`: a `tee` or `tail` in the tail position reports its own status, and #117's failed cluster re-deploy sailed through an `&&` chain that way).
- An accepted behavior delta — ordering, precedence, message bytes — is pinned by a test in the same strike; the PR body discloses what the suite already owns (#113's read-precedence delta reached the merge round disclosed but unpinned, and the merge round paid the pin).
- The review round names every accepted deviation from the spec's letter — additions beyond the enumeration included — with the reason; the disclosure lands in the same strike's PR body, not in a later pass (#127's survey-inputs bullet rode through PR #128's draft review undisclosed, and the triage round paid the disclosure).
- An extraction test — one that pulls structured tokens out of prose — consumes from its anchor: the match opens the claim it pins, leading whitespace only, never searching forward past other text. An unanchored match can borrow a later passage and pass silently (#122's review round caught the prose check's enumeration doing exactly that).
- A spec's acceptance numbers and failure-mode claims are measured before the spec lands — a claim one command can falsify is a delta the strike inherits for free (#120's lint:dups "count drops" claim was false at min-tokens 50: the four mirrors were never token-level clones, and the strike paid the probes to falsify it).
- Secrets ride files — a read-only mount or a `--env-file` — into child processes and containers. An argv element is process-table-visible, so no credential, token, or header value rides one (the M5 S3 review round caught the gateway token on a `docker exec -e`; the preflight env file is the shape).
- When a change supersedes text in a steering doc (`CLAUDE.md`, `GLOSSARY.md`, `docs/adr/`), the same strike edits that text — and superseded means stale by omission as well as false: a section that describes the changed surface covers the new behavior in the same strike (S1's ceiling paragraph was omission-stale through three review passes; only a post-merge strike fixed it).
- A strike that changes a self-authored skill's `SKILL.md` bumps that skill's frontmatter `version:` in the same strike — the field is the skill's own minor, not the package's.
- `.npmrc` pins the official registry (the machine default is npmmirror).
- PR bodies, repo prose, and committed fixtures are public surfaces: cluster account names, SSH aliases, and node names never enter them — they live in `CLAUDE.local.md`, and GitHub keeps body edit history, so a scrub-after is not undo. A committed fixture is the sharpest case — a captured transcript above all: sanitization redacts the payload its tool outputs carry (node lists, job names), not only machine paths; the S2 codemode fixture shipped node lists until a round-2 review caught them. The recipe lives with the golden fixtures in `test/dogfood-audit.test.mjs`. (The cluster's own name is public — ADR 0004 names it.) The Spec review checks.
- No build step; tests use Node's built-in node:test runner (pi loads extension TS via jiti). Verify changes with `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run lint:py` (ruff over the self-authored skill scripts and the gateway tree — vendored trees stay verbatim and out of scope), `npm run lint:sh` (pipefail over the repo's shell surfaces; exceptions argue in the lint), `npm run lint:dups` (jscpd duplication ratchet), and `npm run typecheck`; check shipped files with `npm pack --dry-run`.
- Commits run the suite via the versioned `.githooks/pre-commit` hook; enable it per clone with `git config core.hooksPath .githooks`.
- Dogfood acceptance criteria are met on captured evidence — session transcripts for the skill criteria, recorded exit status and stderr for clean boot — never the model's self-report. Procedure: `docs/agents/dogfood.md`. Dogfood and adversarial sessions run in the clean-room rig (`test/rig/`, ADR 0005): `node test/rig/run.mjs run "<prompt>"`; the provider key and — on a `--gateway` leg — the gateway token are the only credentials that enter it (the cluster SSH key never does; the container reaches the gateway through the host-side port-forward, preflighted in-container before launch), and a gated headless leg runs `--gateway --rpc` — the checked-in confirm driver answers the submit gate.

## Git workflow — one "coding strike" per task

1. Start the strike in a new git worktree on a feature branch. A worktree inside the repo (`.claude/worktrees/`) resolves the checkout's `node_modules`; one placed elsewhere needs `npm ci` first. Files read before entering the worktree carry the old base — re-read anything you are about to anchor-edit, and fetch `origin main` before diffing against or removing the worktree.
2. On the first commit, open a **draft** PR against `main` and run `node scripts/check-strike.mjs <spec#>` from the strike worktree: the evidence leg passes by design at draft time, the review-coverage leg skips while the PR is draft, and the CI leg still exits 1 while a check runs pending — the printed offender line, not the exit code, tells pending from a real failure. The child walk is the draft-time signal: a gate defect or a missing child surfaces with the strike ahead of it, not at ready time (S1's gate read a blocked-by mention as an unlanded child; #61 fixed the detection, and the early run keeps the next defect cheap). Run the strike's review round at draft time too, **before any dogfood capture**: the reviewer sees the diff with the least context pressure, its fixes land while the tree is cheap to change, and the evidence pair then captures once at the final HEAD. The reverse order pays a full recapture every time a review fix moves HEAD — M5 S3 and S4 each paid one on 2026-10-31 (three live legs with cluster toggles; the closeout pair), review-first would have paid neither. Review first, capture once.
3. Commit and push every further change to that PR branch, and refresh the PR body as each strike lands — the body is read mid-flight by reviewers and the owner, not only before ready.
4. Before marking the PR ready, run `node scripts/check-strike.mjs <spec#>` from the strike worktree — every child of the spec issue must be landed on the branch or already closed (a closeout ticket for the post-merge steps is the expected open exception; a childless issue is a maintenance strike). The same gate fails a PR whose body attests dogfood evidence at an SHA that is not HEAD — recapture the pair, never rebind the words — and refuses while any PR check is non-pass, pending included (M3's red `verify` sat four hours past ready; only merge-day habit caught it). Refresh the PR's title and body to cover every landed child, then run the review pass over everything changed since the draft round and disclose each round in the body as a `reviewed: <base>..<head>` line (hex shas, base exclusive; a lone sha names one commit) — the gate's coverage leg refuses a ready PR whose branch commits no disclosed range covers (#133 retro: a fix range merged unreviewed and paid a post-merge triage round) — then mark the PR ready and merge to `main`. For milestone-sized PRs, consider one external-model review round before merge — M2's Codex round caught a defect class two same-model rounds missed.
5. The adversarial loop's stop condition is judgment: once findings require crafted attack strings that honest usage would never produce, stop, record them as a residual trust boundary, and move on. "Findings stay wording-level for two consecutive rounds" applies only to findings a realistic session could trigger; if it has not fired within ~10 rounds, it will not — an adversarial reviewer regenerates findings indefinitely, and "clean" is not a stopping condition it can reach.
6. While a review round is in flight, hold further commits on that branch; when its report arrives, triage against the SHA it reviewed.
7. At teardown, run `node scripts/strike-teardown.mjs <branch>` from anywhere inside the repo — it anchors the main checkout by the shared git dir, refuses unless the branch is merged into `origin/main` (the guard that licenses the `-D`, since plain `-d` compares against the lagging remote topic branch), pulls `main` fast-forward, removes the worktree, and deletes the branch last: the worktree holds it checked out, so the delete refuses until the worktree is gone. A harness-created worktree carries the session's own lock — exit it through the harness's worktree-exit tool before the teardown, or the remove refuses on the lock (the M5 S0 retro). A manual teardown repeats that order with every git command anchored to the main checkout (`git -C <main-checkout>`) — a command run inside the worktree acts on the feature branch (the S4 retro's stray pull fast-forwarded it; the S5 retro repeated the accident), and a session standing in the removed worktree loses its git context (the S3 retro session).

## Publishing

`npm publish` is owner-only (browser 2FA; non-interactive publishes fail with `EOTP`). Prepare the release, commit, push — then stop and let the owner publish. It runs from the repo checkout — the committed `.npmrc` pins `registry.npmjs.org` (the machine default is npmmirror) — and that checkout must be the merged tree first: `git pull --ff-only origin main`, then confirm `package.json`'s version and the `npm pack --dry-run` file count match the release, because the M3 publish ran from a stale checkout (0.2.0, 289 files) and only npm's version-conflict refusal caught it. # Theta compute

The gateway skill: the doctrine for running cluster jobs through the
**compute gateway** (ADR 0004) — the `theta-compute` MCP server wrapping the
Slurm CLI on the cluster's login node. Enforcement (bearer auth, the argument
guard, the path sandbox, one audit line per call) stays server-side; this
skill carries the judgment — when to stage, submit, poll, fetch, and record.
There are no helper scripts here: call the gateway's tools directly.

## Before the first call

The gateway is reached through a port-forward to the login node (phase-0).
If a call fails to connect, the forward is down — tell the researcher; do
not retry in a loop. Setup lives in the package README ("Compute gateway
setup"); the registration is one-time and user-level.

Start every compute task with `list_environments` — it shows the partitions
and their state, and a partition drained or down changes the plan before any
job is staged.

## The lifecycle

One run of the loop, in order:

1. **Stage** — `stage_files(run_name, files)` writes the inputs into the
   run's directory under the staging root. Pick a short, descriptive
   `run_name` (`[A-Za-z0-9_-]`); it names the directory and the job. The
   in-band cap is 32 MiB per call; past it the refusal names the out-of-band
   path — move large inputs (an MSA, a feature directory) into the run
   directory with `scp` and say so in the report.
2. **Submit** — `submit_job(run_name, directives?)` for a raw batch job, or
   `run_alphafold3(run_name, fold_input)` for the typed AlphaFold3 path
   (fold-input JSON in, job out). Either answer carries the `job_id` — the
   handle for everything that follows. Directives stay inside the gateway's
   allow-list and ceilings; the fixed partition/gres defaults are the
   cluster's own production values, so pass directives only when the task
   genuinely needs them.
3. **Poll** — `job_status(job_id)` until the job leaves the queue. Poll
   with discipline (below).
4. **Fetch** — `fetch_artifacts(run_name)` brings the run directory back
   (whole tree by default, named picks when the manifest is known). Same
   in-band cap; oversized outputs ride `scp` out of the run directory.
5. **Record** — close the run out in the project notebook. Assemble the job
   record from the answers in hand — job ID, gateway, run name, template
   (null for a raw submit), argument digest (the sha256 of the job's
   canonical input), final state, and the artifact manifest when
   `fetch_artifacts` answered (paths and sizes; strip the contents) — save
   it as JSON, and append it through `theta-notebook`'s recorder with
   `--method` and `--job-record`, graded `re-executed` when the artifacts
   were fetched and `asserted` otherwise. A recorded job ID is durable —
   any later session can re-fetch its artifacts or cross-check its state
   without this one's memory.

## Poll discipline

- Poll `job_status` at sane intervals; a queued job waits on the scheduler,
  and tight polling changes nothing. Between polls, do other work or end
  the turn — never spin on status calls.
- A job still queued after unusually long (compare `list_environments` for
  partition state) is a report to the researcher, not a reason to resubmit.
- On a failed or unexpected state, read `job_logs(job_id)` before
  concluding anything; the log tail is the evidence.
- Never call `cancel_job` without the researcher's explicit request — it is
  a destructive call and the submit gate prompts for it like a submission.
- Long jobs survive the session: jobs live in Slurm, the session does not.
  A submitted cluster job is a durable run — it outlives the session that
  started it. Record the job ID first, then it is safe to close the laptop;
  a later session resumes from the notebook, polls the same job ID, and
  fetches.

## The submit gate

The package's submit gate extension asks the researcher before every
destructive gateway call — `submit_job`, `cancel_job`, and
`run_alphafold3`. That confirm dialog is part of the flow, not friction:
state what is about to run and let the answer land. A refused call stays
refused — never retry it unprompted. Read-only calls (`job_status`,
`job_logs`, `list_environments`, `fetch_artifacts`) and staging run without
prompts; monitoring stays frictionless.

## The server-side bounds

Two bounds live in the gateway itself, set at deploy time. No session
changes them, and both answer before any job is created.

- **The submit capability** (ADR 0006): while it is off, `submit_job` and
  `run_alphafold3` answer a hard refusal — a HOLD audit line — and
  `cancel_job` with the read-only tools stay in service. On a held
  submission, report the hold to the researcher and stop; the enable is
  out-of-band (the cluster's deploy env), so retrying the call in-session
  changes nothing.
- **The submit ceiling**: one principal may spend only so many submits per
  rolling hour; the deploy env names the number, 20 by default. Past it,
  the same tools answer a throttled refusal — a THROTTLE audit line —
  naming the principal, the count, and the window. The backoff is the
  window itself: wait for it to roll, report the throttle to the
  researcher, and do not resubmit in this session.

Both refusals are answers, not failures to diagnose: the tool call
returned, and the cluster declined to create the job. Spend them neither
on retries nor on workarounds — a staging or polling call cannot reach
what only a submit may.

## Codemode inside compute sessions

pi exposes the gateway's tools to codemode by default, and a session with
the gateway registered runs codemode auto-activated — so a compute task
that writes a script to drive the gateway is the normal case, not a
detour. Every nested call still crosses the tool-call pipeline
(`parentToolCallId` links the layers): the submit gate confirms it like a
direct call, the gate log records it, and the gateway audits it. Scripted
submits spend from the same ceiling as direct ones.

## Boundaries

- Call the gateway's tools directly. No wrapper scripts, no SSH by hand
  while the gateway is up — an SSH session bypasses the audit trail the
  institution requires.
- One `run_name` per compute task; reuse a name only to restage the same
  task's inputs deliberately, never to mix two tasks' files.
- Report the job ID, the final state, and where the artifacts landed in the
  workspace — the researcher must be able to find the run without the
  transcript.

# theta-compute — the Theta compute gateway

The M4 compute gateway (ADR 0004): a FastMCP server that wraps the Slurm
CLI on the cluster's login node and speaks MCP over streamable HTTP. The
research agent calls its tools directly through pi's built-in MCP client;
enforcement — bearer auth, the argument guard, the path sandbox, one
audit line per tool call — stays server-side. This tree is generic code
only: every institutional fact (the token, the user name, the audit
location, the ceilings) rides deploy-time env, and the npm tarball does
not ship it. A deploy-time submit capability (ADR 0006) is the outer
bound around job creation: while it is off, the job-creating tools answer
a hard refusal no client can talk its way past. Inside it, a per-principal
submit ceiling (#94) bounds runaway submits: past the ceiling the same
tools answer a throttled refusal the audit log itself derived.

## Layout

```
gateway/
  pyproject.toml        locked uv environment (fastmcp, Python >= 3.11)
  uv.lock
  pyrightconfig.json     pins Pyright to .venv and Python 3.12 (editor
                        diagnostics; no CI leg runs it)
  theta_compute/
    config.py           deploy-time env -> one validated Config
    auth.py             the static bearer-token verifier
    guard.py            what may become a Slurm argument or a staged path
    staging.py          the staging root's filesystem half — runs, logs,
                        scripts, artifact reads
    audit.py            the JSONL audit trail and its rotation
    slurm.py            sinfo/squeue/sbatch/scancel wrappers — argv only
    templates.py        the template registry: load, validate, render
    server.py           the FastMCP app, audit middleware, tool surface
```

## Run

```sh
cd gateway
uv run --locked python -m theta_compute
```

The first run builds the environment from `uv.lock`. The server binds
loopback by default; an unauthenticated process on the same host is the
only thing it exposes, and phase-0 wants exactly that (reach it through
an SSH port-forward, below).

## Deploy-time environment

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `THETA_COMPUTE_TOKEN` | — (required) | the bearer token; the server refuses to start without one |
| `THETA_COMPUTE_USER` | the OS user | the principal the token belongs to; rides every audit line and the job-name prefix |
| `THETA_COMPUTE_SUBMIT_CAPABILITY` | `on` | `on`/`off` — while `off`, `submit_job` and `run_alphafold3` answer a hard refusal (a HOLD audit line); `cancel_job` and the read-only tools stay in service (ADR 0006) |
| `THETA_COMPUTE_SUBMIT_CEILING` | 20 | the per-principal submit ceiling: submits (`submit_job`, `run_alphafold3`) one principal may spend per rolling window before the gateway throttles (a THROTTLE audit line, spec #94); the window is a code constant (3600 s), not env |
| `THETA_COMPUTE_AUDIT_LOG` | `./theta-compute-audit.jsonl` | audit JSONL path |
| `THETA_COMPUTE_AUDIT_MAX_BYTES` | 10485760 | rotation ceiling in bytes |
| `THETA_COMPUTE_SLURM_TIMEOUT` | 30 | per-command Slurm timeout in seconds |
| `THETA_COMPUTE_STAGING_ROOT` | `~/theta-compute-runs` | the staging root: every run directory lives under it |
| `THETA_COMPUTE_TEMPLATES` | — (unset) | the template registry directory; unset leaves the seven generic tools as the whole surface |
| `THETA_COMPUTE_INBAND_MAX_BYTES` | 33554432 | the in-band transfer cap (32 MiB) for stage and fetch alike |
| `THETA_COMPUTE_PARTITIONS` | `cpu` | the partitions a raw submit may name |
| `THETA_COMPUTE_MAX_WALLTIME` | `24:00:00` | ceiling for `time` |
| `THETA_COMPUTE_MAX_MEM_MB` | 65536 | ceiling for `mem`, in MB |
| `THETA_COMPUTE_MAX_NTASKS` | 16 | ceiling for `ntasks` |
| `THETA_COMPUTE_MAX_CPUS_PER_TASK` | 16 | ceiling for `cpus-per-task` |
| `THETA_COMPUTE_MAX_GPUS` | 1 | ceiling for `gres` (`gpu:N`); 0 removes `gres` from the raw path entirely |
| `THETA_COMPUTE_HOST` | 127.0.0.1 | bind address — keep loopback behind the forward |
| `THETA_COMPUTE_PORT` | 8421 | bind port |

## Tools

Seven generic tools, plus the typed `run_alphafold3` when a template
registry is configured (below). The four read-only ones declare the
read-only hint and run ungated on the theta side; `submit_job`,
`cancel_job`, and `run_alphafold3` declare the destructive hint — the
theta-side submit gate confirms them. All of that sits inside a second,
server-held bound: the submit capability, below.

- **`list_environments`** — every partition-state group sinfo reports
  (`sinfo --noheader --format "%P|%a|%l|%D|%t|%N"`), parsed to records:
  `partition`, `default`, `availability`, `time_limit`, `nodes`, `state`,
  `node_list`.
- **`job_status(job_id)`** — one job's status
  (`squeue --noheader --format "%i|%T|%j|%P|%M|%R" --job <id>`). A job id
  is digits only in v1; a well-formed id the queue does not hold answers
  `{"found": false, "job_id": ...}` — an answer, not an error.
- **`stage_files(run_name, files)`** — write the given files (base64,
  in-band) into `<staging root>/<run_name>/`. The call lands whole or
  not at all: every path resolves and every byte counts against the cap
  before the first write.
- **`submit_job(run_name, directives?)`** — render the run's guarded
  batch script and submit it (`sbatch <script path>`, argv only).
  Answers `{job_id, job_name, script_path}`.
- **`job_logs(job_id, tail_lines?)`** — the job's stdout and stderr from
  its run directory (the forced `--output`/`--error` put them there),
  tailed to the last `tail_lines` (default 100, max 1000). A job no run
  directory holds a log for answers `found: false`.
- **`cancel_job(job_id)`** — cancel one job, after squeue confirms its
  name carries this user's `theta-<user>-` prefix. A well-formed id the
  queue no longer holds answers `{"found": false, "canceled": false}`.
- **`fetch_artifacts(run_name, paths?)`** — read the run directory back
  in-band (base64): the whole tree by default, or the named picks. Whole
  or not at all — every file is read and sized inside the cap before
  anything returns.
- **`run_alphafold3(run_name, fold_input)`** — the typed tool: validate
  the AF3-native fold-input JSON (name, sequences, modelSeeds, dialect
  `"alphafold3"`, version 1), stage its canonical bytes into the run
  directory, render the registered template's free variables only, and
  submit. Answers `{job_id, job_name, script_path, fold_input_path,
  output_dir}`. Registered only when `THETA_COMPUTE_TEMPLATES` is set and
  its registry registers an `alphafold3` template.

## Tool policy

Every tool's policy lives in one co-located record beside its definition
in `server.py` (`ToolPolicy`: the annotations, whether the tool is
job-creating, and its pre-dispatch guard callable). The `@app.tool`
decorator binds its annotations from that record, so the wire's hints are
the record's; the audit middleware reads the same record per call for the
submit capability's hold, the submit ceiling's count, the mutating
surface that carries the observed capability on its audit lines, and the
guard dispatch. `mutating` is not stored — it is exactly the negation of
the read-only hint, so the audit line and the wire cannot disagree.

Boot reconciles the registry against the registered surface and refuses
to start on a mismatch — a tool without a record is a tool the middleware
cannot police; a record without a tool is dead policy. The offline
boundary test holds the same invariant against the source (Python's own
parser, not a regex) and the live `tools/list`, and pins the hold's and
the instructions' words to the job-creating records — those bytes are
frozen on every HOLD audit line (ADR 0006), so they stay literals.

## The submit capability

The outer bound (ADR 0006), deploy-time and server-held: while
`THETA_COMPUTE_SUBMIT_CAPABILITY` is `off`, `submit_job` and
`run_alphafold3` answer a hard refusal — pre-dispatch, before the guard,
with nothing written and nothing run. The refusal is its own audit-line
kind (`decision: "HOLD"`, below), so held submits are countable like
denials, and every mutating tool's line carries the capability the call
observed. `cancel_job` stays in service during a hold — a hold is
exactly when a runaway needs cancelling — and the read-only tools are
unaffected; `tools/list` keeps advertising the held tools, because the
hold is a call-time refusal, not a vanishing surface. The theta-side
confirm gate stays the inner, per-call gate; this one stands even for a
client that bypasses the package.

The capability is boolean-until-off: unset means `on`, and only an
explicit `off` holds. Its state never lives in the process — it is the
deploy env, so a restart of the same deploy keeps it by construction. On
the cluster the state rides `theta-compute.env` beside the deploy (rsync
never touches it), sourced by every start line — deploy.sh and the
runbook below both do it — so a redeploy cannot silently re-enable
submits. Where the file and the start line both name a variable, the
start line's own assignment wins. A hold or an enable is one edit plus
a restart:

```sh
ssh <login-node-alias>
cd <remote-dir>
echo 'THETA_COMPUTE_SUBMIT_CAPABILITY=off' > theta-compute.env   # the hold
# echo 'THETA_COMPUTE_SUBMIT_CAPABILITY=on' > theta-compute.env  # the enable
# then restart with the phase-0 start command (step 3), which sources the file
```

## The submit ceiling

Inside the capability, a rolling per-principal bound on job creation
(spec #94 — ADR 0006's throttle instance): `submit_job` and
`run_alphafold3` may spend at most `THETA_COMPUTE_SUBMIT_CEILING`
submits per rolling 3600-second window. Past it the call answers a
throttled refusal — pre-dispatch like the hold, before the guard — and
the refusal names the principal, the observed count, and the window.
`cancel_job` and the read-only tools neither spend nor face the ceiling:
monitoring and remediation stay frictionless under a throttle exactly as
under a hold.

The count is the audit log's own record, read at call time: the
principal's `ALLOW` lines for the two job-creating tools whose `ts`
falls inside the window. That makes the trail the ceiling's only state —
a restart keeps the count by construction, because it never lived in the
process — and it picks the honest accounting on purpose: a submit Slurm
then refused still counts (the call spent the boundary's dispatch, and a
loop of failing submits is still a loop), while DENY, HOLD, and THROTTLE
lines never count (nothing ran). The window's memory is the trail the
deploy keeps: the current audit file plus its one rotated generation.

Layering keeps one call, one line: the capability is checked first, the
ceiling next, the guard last — a call that would fail several answers
the outermost line, so a hold outranks the ceiling and the ceiling
outranks a guard refusal. Two residuals are on record: the ceiling
observes counts, it is not a semaphore — two submits racing the same
instant can both pass — and a wiped audit log is a reset budget, one
more reason `audit/` is deploy state, never rsynced over.

The ceiling is one or greater — a zero ceiling is the capability's job,
not the throttle's — and rides the same channel as the capability:

```sh
ssh <login-node-alias>
cd <remote-dir>
echo 'THETA_COMPUTE_SUBMIT_CEILING=2' >> theta-compute.env  # a deliberately low test ceiling
# delete the line to restore the default (20); then restart (step 3), which sources the file
```

## The guard: sandbox, allow-list, ceilings

- **Path sandbox.** Every path the tools touch resolves under the
  staging root. Lexical escapes (`..`, absolute paths) refuse at the
  argument guard; symlinks that resolve outside the root refuse at
  resolution; a fetch never follows a symlink out. A run name is
  1–64 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` — a directory name and nothing else.
- **Command guard.** `submit_job` directives are an allow-list, not a
  passthrough: `partition`, `time`, `mem`, `ntasks`, `cpus-per-task`,
  `gres` (`gpu:N`, N ≤ the ceiling). Each value is one token of safe
  characters (no spaces, no newline — nothing that could break out of a
  script line) and each sits under its ceiling. The job name
  (`theta-<user>-<run_name>`, the per-user ownership prefix), the log
  paths (inside the run directory), and the script body are
  gateway-forced: the client controls directives only, never commands —
  commands arrive with templates (S3), never through the raw path.
- **In-band cap.** `stage_files` and `fetch_artifacts` move at most
  `THETA_COMPUTE_INBAND_MAX_BYTES` per call. Past it the refusal names
  the out-of-band path: move the files with scp to (or from) the run
  directory on the cluster — large inputs (an MSA, a feature directory)
  travel that way by design.

## The template registry

Typed tools render institutional job templates — the cluster's own
production scripts, never files in this repo (ADR 0004). The registry is
one deploy-time directory (`THETA_COMPUTE_TEMPLATES`) holding each
template's script beside a `registry.json` manifest:

```json
{
	"alphafold3": {
		"script": "alphafold3.sbatch",
		"free": ["RUN_DIR", "JOB_NAME"],
		"input_file": "af_input/fold_input.json",
		"output_dir": "af_output"
	}
}
```

- **Free variables** are the only client-shaped parts of a rendered
  script, and the vocabulary is closed: `{{RUN_DIR}}` (the run
  directory, absolute — the `cd` and the input/output binds) and
  `{{JOB_NAME}}` (the gateway-forced `theta-<user>-` ownership name).
  A template declares exactly the tokens its script carries; a declared
  token the script never uses, a token the manifest never declared, or a
  name outside the vocabulary refuses at startup.
- **`input_file` and `output_dir`** are paths inside the run directory —
  the manifest's own words must match what the script's fixed text binds
  on the container side; the registry validates the shapes (relative,
  no escapes), the deploy keeps the two consistent.
- **Startup validation.** A missing `registry.json`, invalid JSON, a
  missing script, or a registry that registers no `alphafold3` template
  refuses to boot — the same fail-loudly contract as a missing token.
  A directory that registers only other templates is legal for the
  registry and fatal for the typed tool, which has nothing to render.
- Everything else in the script is fixed text: partition, gres, binds,
  the SIF, the runner line. `run_alphafold3` takes no directives at all
  — any extra argument is an override attempt and a guard refusal.

Spec #49's optional project code is deliberately absent from v1: the
probed production template carries no account line to render it into,
so the closed vocabulary is that decision on record. The vocabulary
grows when an institutional template needs one.

The on-cluster recipe (owner, one time): copy the production af3 template
into the registry directory, replace the run-dir occurrences (the `cd`
and the three run binds) with `{{RUN_DIR}}` and the job name with
`{{JOB_NAME}}`, keep single `fold_input.json` as the input contract, and
write `registry.json` beside it. The probed live template, its drift
findings, and the pinned values (XLA_FLAGS line, platform model and
database paths, the nvidia bind) live on-cluster in the template mirror —
institutional facts, not repo content.

## The audit trail

One JSONL line per tool call, in this byte shape — canonical JSON, sorted
keys, no whitespace (the user value below is illustrative):

```json
{"args_sha256":"sha256:7c5436bc2d8d4ac0751aff3bc8a18e8286be2c420163ad5e22a6062387794e75","decision":"ALLOW","job_id":"1851277","reason":null,"tool":"job_status","ts":"2026-10-21T01:05:08Z","user":"cluster-user"}
```

And a held submit, its own kind (the mutating-only field rides it):

```json
{"args_sha256":"sha256:9a1f…","decision":"HOLD","job_id":null,"reason":"the submit capability is off — job-creating calls (submit_job, run_alphafold3) are held; the enable is out-of-band: the deploy env (theta-compute.env), see gateway/README.md; report the hold to the researcher and do not retry","submit_capability":"off","tool":"submit_job","ts":"2026-10-30T09:15:42Z","user":"cluster-user"}
```

And a throttled submit — the ceiling's own kind, carrying the count and
the window it was taken over (the mutating-only field rides it too):

```json
{"args_sha256":"sha256:3d07…","decision":"THROTTLE","job_id":null,"reason":"the submit ceiling is reached — principal cluster-user has 3 submit(s) in the rolling 3600-second window (ceiling 3); the ceiling is deploy-time env (theta-compute.env on the cluster), see gateway/README.md; wait for the window to roll, report the throttle to the researcher, and do not retry in this session","submit_capability":"on","submit_count":3,"submit_window_seconds":3600,"tool":"submit_job","ts":"2026-10-30T10:41:07Z","user":"cluster-user"}
```

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `ts` | UTC ISO-8601 instant of the decision, second resolution |
| `user` | the authenticated principal the token belongs to |
| `tool` | tool name |
| `args_sha256` | `sha256:<hex>` over the canonical JSON of the argument object (sorted keys, no whitespace) — the digest, never the arguments |
| `decision` | `ALLOW` — the guard let the call through; `DENY` — the guard refused before any subprocess ran; `HOLD` — the submit capability was off, so a job-creating call never reached the guard or a tool (ADR 0006); `THROTTLE` — the principal reached the submit ceiling, so a job-creating call never reached the guard or a tool (spec #94) |
| `job_id` | the call's job-id argument when the tool takes one; else the id a successful `submit_job` minted; on a DENY it is the rejected value verbatim when it was a string (the digest always covers the full arguments) |
| `submit_capability` | `"on"`/`"off"` on lines for mutating tools (`stage_files`, `submit_job`, `cancel_job`, `run_alphafold3`) — the capability the call observed, on every decision; absent on read-only lines |
| `submit_count` | on a THROTTLE line: the submits the log held for the principal inside the window when the call arrived; absent from every other line |
| `submit_window_seconds` | on a THROTTLE line: the rolling window, in seconds, the count was taken over; absent from every other line |
| `reason` | null on success; a DENY names the refusal; an ALLOW that failed names the failure; a HOLD names the hold; a THROTTLE names the principal, the count, and the window |

A call without a valid token is answered HTTP 401 by the transport and is
not a tool call — it leaves no audit line. Rotation keeps one prior
generation: past the byte ceiling the current file becomes `<name>.1`
(replacing any earlier one) and a fresh file starts. An institution that
needs deeper history ships the rotated file out on a schedule.

DENY is strictly pre-dispatch: it covers every refusal decidable from the
arguments alone — shapes, the path sandbox, the directive ceilings, the
in-band cap — and nothing has run when it lands. Refusals that need the
call to run first stay ALLOW with the refusal as the reason: cancelling a
job whose name lacks the ownership prefix (squeue had to answer first),
a fetch past the cap (the run directory had to be read), a symlink in the
fetched tree. The audit trail holds both; the distinction is honest about
what had run. The capability is checked first, the ceiling next, the
guard last: a call that would fail several answers the outermost line —
HOLD over THROTTLE over DENY — one call, one line, and the outer bound is
the one that answered.

# Theta project notebook

The third Theta-owned skill: the recorder for the **project notebook** (ADR
0003) — the durable record of a research effort, accumulating across
sessions and tools in the research project's workspace. A session transcript
dies with the session; the notebook belongs to the project.

## Where the notebook lives

Plain files under `.theta/` in the workspace the session runs in:

- `notebook.jsonl` — one JSON entry per line, **append-only**. Inspect, diff,
  back up, version — no pi runtime needed.
- `evidence/` — sha256-addressed snapshots, one file per evidence item. Same
  bytes, same name: identical evidence stored twice is one file.

## The five entry types

One recorder call appends one entry. Every entry carries its `id` (sequenced
per type), its `type`, the `date` it was recorded, and its `text`.

| Type | Ids | Text flag | Evidence | Also carries |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| hypothesis | `hyp-0001`… | `--hypothesis` | required | — |
| method | `mth-0001`… | `--method` | optional | — |
| observation | `obs-0001`… | `--observation` | required | its own `grade`; items may link |
| decision | `dec-0001`… | `--decision` | optional | — |
| confidence | `cnf-0001`… | `--confidence` | never | the `hypothesis` it judges (`--on`) |

- A hypothesis or an observation is a claim about what a source showed, so
  evidence is required. A method or a decision may stand on the researcher's
  reasoning; record the motivating search as its evidence when one exists.
- A confidence entry is judgment, not a source claim: it takes no evidence,
  and `--on` names the hypothesis entry it judges — recorded later, so the
  judgment history sits next to the evidence it weighs.
- **Evidence-to-hypothesis links**: an observation's evidence item may carry
  `supports: hyp-0001` (`--supports`), marking it as backing an existing
  hypothesis. The recorder refuses a link that names no recorded hypothesis.
  A hypothesis entry's own evidence needs no link — it backs that entry.

A hypothesis entry, and an observation linked to it, from the same notebook:

```json
{
  "id": "hyp-0001",
  "type": "hypothesis",
  "date": "2026-10-19",
  "text": "CRISPR-based gene editing can restore immune cell function in aged organisms",
  "evidence": [
    {
      "source": "pubmed",
      "endpoints": ["esearch.fcgi", "esummary.fcgi"],
      "query": "CRISPR gene therapy",
      "retrieved": "2026-10-18",
      "grade": "asserted",
      "snapshot": "evidence/<sha256>.json"
    }
  ]
}
```

```json
{
  "id": "obs-0001",
  "type": "observation",
  "date": "2026-10-20",
  "text": "Two independent retrievals agree that HDR-mediated repair is rare in HSCs",
  "grade": "cross-checked",
  "evidence": [
    {
      "source": "pubmed",
      "endpoints": ["esearch.fcgi", "esummary.fcgi"],
      "query": "CRISPR gene therapy",
      "retrieved": "2026-10-18",
      "grade": "cross-checked",
      "snapshot": "evidence/<sha256>.json",
      "supports": "hyp-0001"
    }
  ]
}
```

- `date` is the day the entry was recorded; `retrieved` is the day the
  connector made its call (the connector's `provenance.accessed`, carried
  through). Two different claims, both kept.
- The evidence item carries the source, the endpoints called, the query, the
  retrieval date, the grade, and the snapshot address. `query` is the search
  term, or null for an identifier lookup (whose identifiers ride in the
  snapshot itself).
- A **job record** (ADR 0004) is the evidence item of the method entry that
  records a compute run: the gateway as its `source`, the job ID, the
  template (null for a raw submit), the argument digest, the final state,
  and the artifact manifest when the artifacts were fetched. Its `retrieved`
  is the day the record's state was observed. The recorder accepts the grade
  `re-executed` only when the manifest is present.
- The snapshot is the evidence source's structured output byte-for-byte —
  the connector's `--json` output (already credential-redacted and already
  dated by the connector's own code) or the assembled job record. Raw HTTP
  bodies are never kept.

## When to record

- The loop's hypothesize moment: a hypothesis has survived framing and
  search, and the connector output that motivated it is in hand.
- The design moment: a method is chosen or discarded — record the choice,
  with the search that motivated it as evidence when there is one.
- The execute moment: reading a result off a search output is an
  observation; when it backs an existing hypothesis, link the evidence. A
  compute run that closes out records its job record as a method entry —
  the theta-compute doctrine walks the lifecycle.
- Any point a direction is set or cut: a decision, recorded as its own
  entry so the correction of an earlier entry is a later entry, never a
  rewrite of history.
- When judgment moves: a confidence entry on a named hypothesis — raised,
  lowered, or held, with the reasoning in the text.
- A standalone literature search outside the orchestrator loop that lands a
  claim worth keeping — any session that finds evidence leaves its trace.
- Record only through this skill's script. Never edit `notebook.jsonl` by
  hand; the recorder refuses to append to a notebook it cannot parse, and
  append-only is the format's contract.

## Operations

The recorder writes `.theta/` under the **current directory**, so run it with
the research project's workspace as the cwd — never from inside the skill
tree, which would land the notebook in the package checkout. Resolve the
script path against the skill directory (pi's rule for skill-relative paths)
and pass it absolute:

```bash
cd /path/to/research-project

# The real flow — a hypothesis off a live search, piped straight in:
python3 <theta-lit-search-skill-dir>/scripts/pubmed.py --query "CRISPR gene therapy" --json | \
  python3 <theta-notebook-skill-dir>/scripts/notebook.py \
  --hypothesis "TEXT" --evidence - --grade asserted

# The chosen method, with the search that motivated it:
python3 <theta-notebook-skill-dir>/scripts/notebook.py \
  --method "TEXT" --evidence search.json --grade asserted

# An observation, its evidence linked to the hypothesis it supports:
python3 <theta-notebook-skill-dir>/scripts/notebook.py \
  --observation "TEXT" --evidence search.json --grade cross-checked --supports hyp-0001

# A decision (no evidence needed), and a confidence judgment:
python3 <theta-notebook-skill-dir>/scripts/notebook.py --decision "TEXT"
python3 <theta-notebook-skill-dir>/scripts/notebook.py \
  --confidence "TEXT" --on hyp-0001

# A compute run closes out: the assembled job record rides a method entry
# (theta-compute's doctrine assembles it from the gateway answers):
python3 <theta-notebook-skill-dir>/scripts/notebook.py \
  --method "TEXT" --job-record job-record.json --grade re-executed
```

`--evidence` takes the path of a saved `--json` output, or `-` to read it
from stdin; `--job-record` takes an assembled gateway job record the same
way. The two are mutually exclusive — one evidence item per call — and
`--grade` is required exactly when either is given. `--on` and `--supports`
must name a hypothesis entry already in the notebook; a reference that names
no recorded hypothesis is a usage error, never an entry.

Requires Python 3.11+ (standard library only). If `python3` is older, run
`python3.13`, `python3.12`, or `python3.11` — the script names them when the
gate trips. Default output is the recorded line, then the entry's specifics
— the evidence item's source and retrieval date with its grade, and the
snapshot address; `--json` prints the appended entry itself instead.

### The job record's shape

The session assembles the record from the theta-compute answers for one run
and passes it to `--job-record` as JSON (path or `-`):

```json
{
  "gateway": "theta-compute",
  "job_id": "12347",
  "run_name": "af3-lysozyme",
  "template": "alphafold3",
  "arguments_digest": "<sha256 of the job's canonical input>",
  "state": "COMPLETED",
  "observed": "2026-10-25",
  "artifacts": {"run_name": "af3-lysozyme", "total_bytes": 49414,
                "files": [{"path": "alphafold3_output/model.cif", "size": 48211}]}
}
```
